content:
I will only mention points that have not already been raised by others.

Every current case lists tower positions in ascending order, although Input does not guarantee that order. Please include shuffled positions in both the public and hidden suites. For example, this permutation of the first example must still output 8:

20 2
15 3
5 3

The uncovered length must depend on the coverage intervals, not the order in which towers are supplied. A public/hidden pair with shuffled, overlapping intervals would test that property more thoroughly.

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: The issues have not been fixed. Refer to 5DN1L's first comment for details.

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: The issues mentioned haven't yet been addressed, with the main ones being:

* The test and validator in each pair aren't sufficiently similar

* Inadequate scenario coverage across the cases

* Lack of statement formatting

Formatting
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Goal
* Please format all instances of L and N as [[variables]].

* Please format the first instance of 0 as a {{constant}}.

* Please change the second sentence to:

A tower at position [[P]] with radius [[R]] covers all positions from [[P]] - [[R]] to [[P]] + [[R]], inclusive, clipped to the road from {{0}} through [[L]].

* Consider changing "NOT" to "<<not>>".

Input
* Please format all instances of L and N as [[variables]].

* Please format "Line 1" and "Next [[N]] lines" in <<bold>>.

* Please insert "space-separated" between "two" and "integers" in both descriptions.

* Please change "(road length, number of towers)" to "for the road length and the number of towers respectively".

* Please change "P[i] and R[i] (tower position and radius)" to "[[P]] and [[R]] for the position and radius of a tower respectively".

Constraints
* Please format all [[variables]].

* Please change "P[i]" to "[[P]]".

* Please change "R[i]" to "[[R]]".

* Please change 1000 to 10 as [[N]] never exceeds 10.

* Please change 100000 to 1000 as [[L]] never exceeds 1000.

Game modes
* Do you think it's possible to infer the task based on visible cases alone in Reverse mode, when the problem statement is hidden?

Cases
* Each test and its validator should cover the same scenario with slightly different inputs and outputs whenever possible. Hence, please revise the cases as follows:

  • Create a new validator to pair with the existing Test 1: no overlapping coverage, with one tower's coverage clipped on the left.

  • Pair Validator 1 with Test 2.

  • Create a new test to pair with the existing Validator 2: [[P]] of one tower is 0, and the other tower's coverage boundary touches position [[L]].

  • Create a new validator to pair with the existing Test 3: overlapping coverage of two towers.

  • Create a new test to pair with the existing Validator 3: touching coverage boundaries of two towers, with one tower's coverage clipped on the right.

  • Create a new validator to pair with the existing Test 4: N = 0.

  • Create a new test to pair with the existing Validator 4: R = 0 for all towers.

* Create a new test/validator pair that contains all of the following:

  • [[P]] of one tower is at position 0.

  • [[P]] of one tower is at position [[L]].

  • The coverage of two towers (excluding the tower at position 0) gets clipped on the left.

  • The coverage of two towers (excluding the tower at position [[L]]) gets clipped on the right.

  • The coverage of any three towers overlaps.

  • The coverage boundaries of two towers touch at exactly one position.

  • The output is greater than 0.

* Create another test/validator pair that is the same as the pair above, except that the output is 0.

Thanks.
